issue: The HTTP deadline releases the caller while a worker can remain blocked inside a read. issue: Doc classifier/extractor call the registry with `JsonObject` (wire schema `{"type":"object"}`) and skip `require_strict_schema`. The spec says to reject unexpected schema keys and check the caller's schema, but for doc this check is bypassed by design and doc coerces fields itself.

Unrequested transport behaviour change in the doc LLM path. HTTP redirects are no longer followed (`allow_redirects=False`, redirect becomes an `exit` error). The old `requests.post` followed them. There is also a new 4 MiB reply cap, and a process-group kill with a 5 s reader join for CLIs. The CHANGELOG discloses the redirect change, but the spec asks for behaviour-preserving doc cutover and lists none of these.

`extraction_method` and retry keys change meaning in named mode (`llm:<backend name>` instead of `llm:<model>`). Timeouts now appear as `[timeout] <backend>: ...` in triage reasons instead of the `requests` message. Both are documented and defensible, but neither is in the spec.

A configured `llm:` entry named `ollama` or `llamacpp` silently takes over legacy mode, so `endpoint`/`primary_model`/`fallback_model` are ignored. Docs mention it (docs/source/tools/bim.rst:1063) but nothing warns at load time.

Configuration accepts embedded NULs in command arguments, and `Popen` raises an uncaught `ValueError`. Temporary-directory creation and cleanup can also raise raw `OSError`. Reject NULs at config load and map filesystem failures to `exit`. Add tests for both paths.

Inner JSON decoding can leak `ValueError` for integers above Python's conversion limit and `RecursionError` for deeply nested replies. Both inputs fit the reply cap. Map these decoder failures to `parse` in the shared helper and add regression cases.

The CLI runner ignores the stdin writer's lifetime and checks its errors without joining it. Include the writer in the existing bounded join so pipe failures reach the caller reliably. Decode diagnostic output only on the nonzero-exit path.

The nonzero-exit fallback copies arbitrary command stdout into the error. A command that echoes its input can put OCR text in doc triage reasons. Keep generic command diagnostics on stderr and handle Claude's stdout error envelope in its adapter.
The doc transport tests repeat the fake Requests exception hierarchy and streamed response across six files. Share a test helper and remove fake `.json()` methods where only `iter_content()` is used.

issue: On thread-start failure, killing and reaping the child closes its pipe ends. Parent-side streams assigned to threads that never started can stay open while the chained exception retains the runner frame. Close the unclaimed streams in the failure path and assert closure for each of the three injected startup failures.

The regression fixture sends `SIGKILL` to recorded PIDs even after the runner has reaped them. A reused PID can belong to an unrelated process. Keep the `Popen` handles, assert the runner reaped the test child, and terminate and wait only for a child that is still running. This also removes the `_gone` polling helper.

Both new missing-executable cases pass against the previous implementation because they return before executable resolution changes. Move the relative missing-path case into the existing missing-executable test and remove the duplicate test.

The new promote wiring test repeats the dependency-failure test's setup and invocation. Parameterize the existing test with legacy and named settings so both cases check the forwarded map, the exit status, and the diagnostic.

The `openai` kind sends no Authorization header and the settings have no key field, so an authenticated OpenAI-compatible endpoint cannot be used. The endpoint string is not validated at all. The PRD does not require auth, so this is a limitation.

The pipeline docstring still says `requests.exceptions.Timeout` is re-raised unwrapped. The code now raises `BackendError(TIMEOUT)`. It stays non-transient, so the retry short-circuit still works. Only the comment is stale.

Error-message wording changed for HTTP failures. The old text was "HTTP error calling {url}: ..." and the new text is "HTTP error calling {backend}: ...". Timeouts now read "[timeout] <backend>: ..." in triage reasons. The CHANGELOG lists the timeout change. Tests may pin the new text. Result shapes and the transient/semantic split are unchanged.

The extra hardening goes beyond the PRD text: a 4 MiB reply cap, process-group kill, a 64 KiB stderr cap, a worker-thread total deadline, and a separate `test_llm_transport_hardening.py`. It is defensible as "bounded execution" and I found no defect in it. It is still unrequested surface.
